title: First Manager Launchpad — Hire & Onboard Cookbook
content:
Purpose:
This concise workbook is intended for People Ops, hiring managers, and interview panels to standardize hiring, interviewing, and the first 90-day onboarding for engineers being promoted or hired into their first manager role at Redwood Inference. Focus is on predictable assessment signals, low-friction ramp, mentor rotation, and measurable role-readiness gates.

Scope:
- Applies to first-line manager hires (IC->Manager or external individual contributors without prior people-management experience) for engineering, product, and infra-adjacent teams.
- Includes: hiring profile, interview loop, scoring rubric, sample questions, pre-boarding checklist, day-1/week-1/30/60/90 onboarding milestones, mentor rotation schedule, success gates, and open decisions.

Hiring profile (role snapshot):
- Title example: Engineering Manager I / Product Engineering Lead (IC->MGR path)
- Band: L4-L5 depending on scope
- Core expectations (first 90 days): build trust with direct reports, run weekly 1:1s, lead one small cross-functional deliverable, clear feedback cadence, hand off technical ownership while ensuring delivery quality.

Interview loop (recommended, 4-stage):
1) Hiring mgr screen (30m) — culture fit, motivations, career goals, basic scenario for people preference.
2) Technical leadership (60m) — system design + delegation signals (panel includes tech lead).
3) Manager simulation (60m) — roleplay: performance feedback + prioritization exercise.
4) Team fit + bar-raising (45m) — peers + cross-functional partner.
Decision timeline: aim for 2 weeks from screen to hire decision for internal candidates; 3 weeks for external.

Rubric (4-point anchors; score each area 1-4):
- People Leadership (clearer transition signals): 1 = no experience or unsafe framing, 2 = coaching w/ supervision, 3 = independent coaching of peers, 4 = proactive development plans for team.
- Communication & Stakeholder Mgmt: 1 = opaque updates, 2 = reactive comms, 3 = anticipates blockers, 4 = convinces exec & aligns cross-team priorities.
- Execution & Delegation: 1 = sole doer mindset, 2 = delegates but tracks poorly, 3 = delegates with clear acceptance criteria, 4 = designs team processes to scale.
- Technical Credibility: 1 = limited domain knowledge, 2 = competent contributor, 3 = trusted tech partner, 4 = influences architecture decisions.
- Bias for Learning & Coaching: 1 = no examples, 2 = ad-hoc mentorship, 3 = recurring coaching sessions, 4 = measurable growth outcomes from mentees.
Pass thresholds (panel): must score >=3 in two of (People Leadership, Execution) and no 1s in any critical area. Hiring manager sets final calibration.

Sample questions (with what to listen for):
- Tell me about a time you gave difficult feedback to a peer. What was the outcome? (listen for clarity, follow-up, growth plan)
- Walk me through how you decided who owned a recent project and how you tracked its progress. (look for delegation + acceptance criteria)
- Roleplay: a direct report missed a sprint goal due to poor estimation. How do you approach a 1:1 and a team retro? (listen for accountability + psychological safety)
- How do you coach a strong IC who resists taking on mentoring responsibilities? (probe influence & incentives)

Pre-boarding (complete before day 1):
- Offer packet signed, manager intro note sent, org chart and team one-pager shared.
- IT ticket created (laptop spec, software licensing).
- Access requests: GitHub org, CI/CD, cloud dev project (least privilege initially), Slack, HR systems.
- Assign onboarding mentor and shadow seat for first 30 days.

Day 1 checklist:
- Welcome + role orientation with hiring manager (45m): expectations, first 30/60/90 outcomes, 1:1 cadence.
- HR admin (payroll, benefits) and security briefing.
- Team lunch (virtual/in-person) + team norms doc shared.
- Mentor intro + buddy pairing.

Week 1:
- Read: team roadmap, recent postmortems, current sprint board.
- Observe 1:1s and standups as shadow.
- Small onboarding task assigned (low-risk ownership) with a clear PR/merge expectation.
- Initial manager feedback check-in at EOW (30m).

First 30 days (metrics + milestones):
- Hold regular 1:1s and set development goals for each direct report.
- Complete 2 shadow coaching sessions with mentor observing.
- Deliver small cross-team coordination (document + champion one decision).
- HR checkpoint: review career ladder & promotion criteria with People Ops.

30–60 days:
- Run first performance calibration input for direct reports (feed into peer review process).
- Lead a small retro on a team process and implement 1 improvement.
- Mentor rotation: rotate mentor weekly — Week 5: engineering lead, Week 6: product partner, Week 7: SRE/infra partner.

60–90 days (readiness gates):
- Demonstrate delegation by delivering a project via direct reports (manager operated as unblocker, not main implementer).
- Show measurable improvements in team health (one short survey/qualitative feedback + manager note).
- Manager & People Ops 90-day calibration: go/no-go on full people-manager responsibilities or continued co-lead for next 90 days.

Mentor rotation template (weeks 2–8):
- 1:1 with mentor (30m) — focus on coaching reflection.
- Shadow session (mentor sits in on 1:1 with an IC) every 2 weeks.
- Mentor writes a short note at weeks 4 and 8 with observed strengths & recommended focus areas.

Delegation handoff checklist (for each workstream):
- Clear outcome & success metrics defined.
- Acceptance criteria & test plan documented.
- Stakeholder list + escalation path created.
- Handoff retro scheduled in 2 weeks.

Security & equipment checklist:
- Laptop delivered & encrypted, MFA enabled, VPN access validated.
- Accesses provisioned within 48 hours: GitHub, Redwood infra dev project, alerting dashboards (read-only until gate), HRIS.

Evaluation & success metrics (People Ops + Hiring Manager):
- Quantitative: time to first effective delegation (days), number of 1:1s held, backlog health for owned deliverable.
- Qualitative: direct report feedback, cross-functional partner feedback, mentor short notes.

Open decisions & tuning notes:
- Should we require a formal shadow period for external hires? (pros/cons noted; recommend 30 days mandatory for external candidates).
- Calibration scale: using 1-4 works for speed but panels need 15–20m calibration before debriefs.

Appendix (templates to copy):
- 1:1 agenda template, development plan one-pager, mentor short note template, manager handoff retro template (links in linked_artifacts).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is designed to be low-friction: prioritize observed behavior over resume signals. Strong emphasis on coaching and delegation as leading indicators for manager success. Please add comments inline for specific team variations (product vs infra).
